title: John Stonehouse | The Politician Who Faked His Death
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 哈喽，大家好，欢迎收听 Leonardo English 的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: The show where you can listen to fascinating stories, and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 在这个节目中，你可以听到引人入胜的故事，在提高英语水平的同时，了解世界上各种奇妙而怪异的事物。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about the story of a man called John Stonehouse.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊的是一个叫 John Stonehouse 的人的故事。

sentences.en: He was a charismatic British politician, once even tipped to be Prime Minister, who made a series of very bad decisions.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一位充满魅力的英国政治家，甚至一度被看好会成为首相，但他却做出了一系列非常糟糕的决定。

sentences.en: I won’t give too much away, but this is a story that involves politics, the cold war, sexual affairs, secrets, spies, a beach in Miami and more.
sentences.zh: 我不会透露太多，但这个故事涉及政治、冷战、婚外情、秘密、间谍、迈阿密海滩等等。

sentences.en: OK then, the story of John Stonehouse. In the winter of 1974, Britain was a nation grappling with uncertainty and upheaval.
sentences.zh: 好了，开始讲 John Stonehouse 的故事。1974 年冬天，英国正处于一个充满不确定性和动荡的时期。

sentences.en: It was a time of economic strife and political instability, which saw two general elections in the same year.
sentences.zh: 那是一个经济困难、政治不稳的时代，同年举行了两次大选。

sentences.en: Labour’s Harold Wilson had managed to secure a tenuous grip on power in October, following a hung parliament in February.
sentences.zh: 继 2 月份出现悬浮议会后，工党的 Harold Wilson 在 10 月份勉强保住了政权。

sentences.en: The spectre of industrial action loomed large, with miners’ strikes crippling the nation and leading to the implementation of the three-day working week in an attempt to conserve electricity.
sentences.zh: 罢工潮的阴影笼罩着全国，矿工罢工使国家陷入瘫痪，为了节约用电，政府甚至实施了每周三天工作制。

sentences.en: Amidst this backdrop of turmoil, two high-profile disappearances captured the public’s imagination and dominated newspaper headlines.
sentences.zh: 在这种动荡的背景下，两起备受瞩目的失踪案引发了公众的无限遐想，并占据了报纸头条。

sentences.en: The first was one you may remember from episode number 354, or indeed from a recent interview I did on Luke’s English Podcast, that of Lord Lucan.
sentences.zh: 第一起你可能还记得，我在第 354 期节目中提到过，或者是在我最近接受 Luke’s English Podcast 采访时聊到的，那就是 Lord Lucan 失踪案。

sentences.en: He was the aristocratic gambler who vanished in November 1974 following the brutal murder of his children’s nanny, Sandra Rivett.
sentences.zh: 他是一位贵族赌徒，在 1974 年 11 月他孩子的保姆 Sandra Rivett 惨遭杀害后失踪了。

sentences.en: Lucan’s car was found abandoned, spattered with blood, but the man himself seemed to have vanished into thin air.
sentences.zh: Lucan 的车被发现遗弃在路边，车上血迹斑斑，但他本人却似乎人间蒸发了。

sentences.en: Just 12 days later, in November 1974, the nation was stunned once more when John Stonehouse, a former Labour minister and MP, mysteriously disappeared.
sentences.zh: 仅仅 12 天后，也就是 1974 年 11 月，前工党部长兼国会议员 John Stonehouse 神秘失踪，再次震惊全国。

sentences.en: Stonehouse was presumed drowned, or even eaten by sharks, after his clothes were found neatly folded on a Miami beach.
sentences.zh: 在迈阿密海滩上发现了 Stonehouse 整齐叠放的衣服后，人们推测他溺水身亡，甚至可能被鲨鱼吃掉了。

sentences.en: Both men had disappeared into thin air. Had they died at sea in tragic accidents, had they killed themselves out of shame of what they had done?
sentences.zh: 两个人都人间蒸发了。他们是死于海上意外，还是因为羞愧而自杀？

sentences.en: Or was there another explanation? The case of John Stonehouse seemed to be more clear cut, more obvious, and indeed he was declared dead, and his obituary was published in the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 还是另有隐情？John Stonehouse 的案子看起来更明确、更显而易见，事实上他已被宣布死亡，报纸上也刊登了他的讣告。

sentences.en: The case of Lord Lucan was less so, and he was the chief suspect in a brutal murder.
sentences.zh: Lord Lucan 的案子则没那么简单，他是那起残忍谋杀案的首要嫌疑人。

sentences.en: Police around the world were told to keep a look out for a tall, handsome British man with a smooth, polished accent.
sentences.zh: 全球警察都接到通知，要留意一名身材高大、长相英俊、操着一口流利考究口音的英国男子。

sentences.en: He might have changed appearance, he might have even changed name, and he would probably be behaving in an unusual way.
sentences.zh: 他可能改变了容貌，甚至改了名字，而且举止可能有些反常。

sentences.en: On the other side of the world, in Melbourne Australia, in December of 1974, a bank clerk did notice something a little odd.
sentences.zh: 在地球的另一端，1974 年 12 月的澳大利亚墨尔本，一名银行职员确实注意到了一些奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: A tall and handsome British man had come into the bank one day and made a large withdrawal, only to stroll across the street and go into another bank.
sentences.zh: 一名高大英俊的英国男子有一天来到银行取了一大笔钱，然后径直穿过马路进了另一家银行。

sentences.en: The man had given his name as Clive Mildoon, and he seemed to have all of the required documents.
sentences.zh: 该男子自称 Clive Mildoon，而且似乎带齐了所有必要的文件。

sentences.en: But something seemed off, something just didn’t feel right.
sentences.zh: 但有些事情似乎不太对劲，感觉就是不对。

sentences.en: She asked around and heard from an associate working in the other bank that the tall Englishman had given his name as “Joseph Markham”, not Clive Mildoon, but again he seemed to have all of the required documents.
sentences.zh: 她四处打听，从另一家银行的同事那里听说，那个高个子英国人自称“Joseph Markham”，而不是 Clive Mildoon，但他同样带齐了所有必要的文件。

sentences.en: The teller had read about the murdered nanny and the fugitive British aristocrat, and suspected “Clive Mildoon” and “Joseph Markham” were in fact Lord Lucan.
sentences.zh: 柜员读过关于保姆被杀和英国贵族潜逃的新闻，怀疑“Clive Mildoon”和“Joseph Markham”实际上就是 Lord Lucan。

sentences.en: She called the police, and several days later the tall, handsome man was tracked down and stopped by the police.
sentences.zh: 她报了警，几天后，那名高大英俊的男子被警方追踪并拦截。

sentences.en: The Australians had contacted their British counterparts before making the arrest, to ask how they could confirm whether it was indeed Lord Lucan.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚警方在实施逮捕前联系了英国同行，询问如何确认此人是否真的是 Lord Lucan。

sentences.en: There was a way, they had been told. Ask him to pull down his trousers, the British police instructed them.
sentences.zh: 英国警方指示说，有一个办法：让他脱下裤子。

sentences.en: Lucan had a large scar, 30 centimetres long, on his right thigh.
sentences.zh: Lucan 的右大腿上有一条 30 厘米长的巨大疤痕。

sentences.en: Nobody could cover that up. Find the scar and you’ve found Lucan.
sentences.zh: 谁也掩盖不了这一点。找到疤痕，就找到了 Lucan。

sentences.en: So the Australian police politely asked this man, Clive Mildoon, to pull down his trousers.
sentences.zh: 于是，澳大利亚警察礼貌地要求这个叫 Clive Mildoon 的男人脱下裤子。

sentences.en: To their surprise, there was no scar. The man was not Lord Lucan, but if he wasn’t the disappeared suspected murderer, who was he?
sentences.zh: 令他们惊讶的是，没有疤痕。这人不是 Lord Lucan，但如果他不是那个失踪的杀人嫌犯，那他是谁？

sentences.en: It was only after they consulted photographs of the other high-profile disappearance that year that they made the connection.
sentences.zh: 直到他们查阅了当年另一起备受关注的失踪案的照片后，才把两者联系起来。

sentences.en: Clive Mildoon was the spitting image, he was an exact match, for John Stonehouse, the Labour politician who had either drowned or been eaten by sharks off the coast of Miami a month prior.
sentences.zh: Clive Mildoon 简直和 John Stonehouse 一模一样，完全吻合。而这位工党政治家一个月前刚在迈阿密海岸溺水或被鲨鱼吃掉。

sentences.en: Upon further questioning, Clive Mildoon cracked.
sentences.zh: 经过进一步审问，Clive Mildoon 招供了。

sentences.en: Or rather, John Stonehouse admitted that there was no Mildoon.
sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，John Stonehouse 承认根本没有 Mildoon 这个人。

sentences.en: He had faked his own death and had been living in Australia under a fake name.
sentences.zh: 他伪造了自己的死亡，并一直以假名住在澳大利亚。

sentences.en: He was brought back to Britain, bizarrely was allowed to continue as a member of parliament before being sent to prison a year and a half later.
sentences.zh: 他被带回英国，离奇的是，在一年半后入狱之前，他竟然被允许继续担任国会议员。

sentences.en: And to think, this was a man who many had tipped to become the British Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 想想看，这曾是一个被许多人看好会成为英国首相的人。

sentences.en: According to his university classmates, he had had his eyes set on the top job since he was a young man.
sentences.zh: 据他的大学同学说，他从年轻时起就瞄准了最高职位。

sentences.en: He came from a politically active family - his father was a trade union leader and his mother was the mayor of Southampton, a city on the south coast of England.
sentences.zh: 他出身于一个政治活跃的家庭——父亲是工会领袖，母亲是英格兰南岸城市南安普敦的市长。

sentences.en: John Stonehouse had strong political beliefs from a young age, and joined the British Labour party at the age of 16.
sentences.zh: John Stonehouse 从小就有坚定的政治信念， 16 岁就加入了英国工党。

sentences.en: After a stint in Uganda, where he worked with co-operative businesses, he entered the world of politics, and successfully won a seat as an MP, a member of parliament, at the age of 32.
sentences.zh: 在乌干达工作了一段时间（与合作社企业合作）后，他步入政坛，并在 32 岁时成功当选为国会议员（MP）。

sentences.en: He was charismatic, decisive, and principled.
sentences.zh: 他很有魅力，果断且有原则。

sentences.en: People hung on his every word, and soon he found that people clung to him, believing that this was not just a future leader of the Labour party, but a future British Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 人们对他言听计从，很快他发现人们都追随他，相信他不仅是工党未来的领袖，更是未来的英国首相。

sentences.en: His political rise was not stellar, but he was rewarded with increasing responsibility.
sentences.zh: 他的仕途虽然不算飞黄腾达，但也稳步上升，承担的责任越来越重。

sentences.en: He became the Minister of State for Technology and then something called the “Postmaster General”, which was a political role related to the post office.
sentences.zh: 他先后担任过技术部国务大臣，以及所谓的“邮政总局局长”，这是一个与邮政相关的政治职务。

sentences.en: When the Labour party then lost the election in 1970 his ministerial career was over, but he remained a member of parliament, representing the constituency of Wednesbury, in north Birmingham.
sentences.zh: 1970 年工党在大选中失利，他的部长生涯随之结束，但他仍保留了国会议员身份，代表伯明翰北部的 Wednesbury 选区。

sentences.en: He also had a busy life outside of politics.
sentences.zh: 他在政治之外的生活也很忙碌。

sentences.en: He had got involved in numerous business interests, even attempting to start his own bank and profit from London’s property boom.
sentences.zh: 他涉足了众多商业利益，甚至试图创办自己的银行，并从伦敦的房地产繁荣中获利。

sentences.en: He was well-known around London for his snappy style, being well-dressed, good looking and stylish, and he had all of the trimmings of a wealthy and successful businessman.
sentences.zh: 他在伦敦以干练的风格著称，穿着讲究、长相英俊、时髦，具备了富有且成功的商人所拥有的一切外在特征。

sentences.en: But a combination of bad luck and poor judgement had meant that several of these businesses were heavily in debt, and Stonehouse owed today’s equivalent of millions of pounds.
sentences.zh: 但由于运气不佳和判断失误，他的几家公司负债累累，Stonehouse 欠下的债务相当于今天的数百万英镑。

sentences.en: He might have looked the part, but his finances were a mess.
sentences.zh: 他外表看起来很体面，但财务状况却一团糟。

sentences.en: On a personal level, he had also made some bad decisions.
sentences.zh: 在个人生活方面，他也做出了一些错误的决定。

sentences.en: He had been married since 1948, since he was 23.
sentences.zh: 他从 1948 年起就结婚了，当时他 23 岁。

sentences.en: His wife had stood by him while he pursued his political ambitions, and the pair had two daughters together.
sentences.zh: 在他追求政治抱负的过程中，妻子一直支持他，两人育有两个女儿。

sentences.en: But some time in the late 1960s he had started an affair with his secretary, a woman 21 years his junior.
sentences.zh: 但在 20 世纪 60 年代末的某个时候，他开始与比他小 21 岁的秘书发生婚外情。

sentences.en: His wife had discovered the affair, was understandably furious, and had threatened to leave him.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子发现了这段私情，自然是勃然大怒，并威胁要离开他。

sentences.en: So, he was in deep financial trouble, his marriage was in tatters, and he was having a now open affair with his secretary, who he had refused to leave even after his wife had discovered the affair.
sentences.zh: 于是，他陷入了严重的财务困境，婚姻破裂，而且他与秘书的私情也公开化了，即便妻子发现后他也拒绝离开那个女人。

sentences.en: His political ambitions had also been scuppered, they were over, because the then Labour leader, Harold Wilson, had decided that Stonehouse was “corruptible”, that he could be corrupted.
sentences.zh: 他的政治抱负也破灭了，彻底结束了，因为当时的工党领袖 Harold Wilson 认为 Stonehouse 是“可以被收买的”，也就是容易腐败。

sentences.en: And it is here that we must go into some controversial territory.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们要进入一些有争议的领域。

sentences.en: It would later be alleged that Stonehouse had been spying for Czechoslovakia since the late 1960s.
sentences.zh: 后来有人指控 Stonehouse 从 60 年代末就开始为捷克斯洛伐克当间谍。

sentences.en: He had been passing the Czechs information about British technology, he had been asking questions in parliament that his Czech handlers had passed him, he was a full-on spy, although it was never agreed how effective a spy he was.
sentences.zh: 他一直向捷克人传递有关英国技术的情报，还在议会中提出捷克上线交给他的问题。他是个彻头彻尾的间谍，尽管关于他这个间谍到底有多大作用，人们一直没有定论。

sentences.en: He had, reportedly, been targeted right at the start of his political career because the Czechoslovakian intelligence agency had thought that this was a man who was “on the up”, someone who could in theory ascend right to the top of British politics, becoming Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 据报道，他在政治生涯初期就被盯上了，因为捷克斯洛伐克情报机构认为这是一个“冉冉升起的新星”，理论上可以爬到英国政坛的顶峰，成为首相。

sentences.en: If they got him young, then by the time he was at the top he would be an invaluable asset.
sentences.zh: 如果趁他年轻时就拉拢他，那么等他登上高位时，他将成为一笔无价的资产。

sentences.en: He had, again reportedly, been compromised because Czechoslovakian intelligence agents had taken photographs of him in bed with another woman, and had threatened to show these to his wife.
sentences.zh: 同样据报道，他之所以妥协，是因为捷克斯洛伐克情报人员拍到了他与其他女人在床上的照片，并威胁要给他的妻子看。

sentences.en: What’s more, they had paid him handsomely, which partially helped explain his unusually lavish lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 此外，他们还给了他丰厚的报酬，这在一定程度上解释了他异常奢华的生活方式。

sentences.en: Now, I should add that he always denied this, and his daughter vehemently denied it in a book from 2021.
sentences.zh: 我应该补充一点，他始终否认这一点，他的女儿在 2021 年出版的一本书中也极力否认。

sentences.en: He was no spy, she says, he was a “rabid anti-communist”, and the claims that he was one come from his political enemies.
sentences.zh: 她说他不是间谍，而是一个“狂热的反共分子”，那些指控他的人都是他的政敌。

sentences.en: Unfortunately for Stonehouse, and for his daughter, there is some evidence to suggest that he was passing secrets to the Czechs.
sentences.zh: 对 Stonehouse 和他的女儿来说不幸的是，有一些证据表明他确实向捷克人传递过秘密。

sentences.en: There is a photograph of him strolling around London with a well-known Czech spy, and there is the testimony of a high-ranking Czech spy, who had no discernible motive to lie.
sentences.zh: 有一张他与一名著名的捷克间谍在伦敦散步的照片，还有一名捷克高级间谍的证词，而那个人并没有明显的撒谎动机。

sentences.en: Anyway, spy or no spy, John Stonehouse was in a bit of a pickle by 1974.
sentences.zh: 无论是不是间谍，到 1974 年，John Stonehouse 的处境都非常糟糕。

sentences.en: He was drowning in debt, and was at risk of having to declare personal bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 他债台高筑，面临着不得不宣布个人破产的风险。

sentences.en: And the UK isn’t quite as forgiving as countries like the United States when it comes to bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 在破产问题上，英国并不像美国等国家那样宽容。

sentences.en: If you declare bankruptcy in the UK there are several things you cannot do, including stand as an MP, as a member of parliament.
sentences.zh: 在英国，如果你宣布破产，有很多事情你就不能做了，包括竞选或担任国会议员。

sentences.en: So this was the backdrop to the “disappearance” of John Stonehouse.
sentences.zh: 这就是 John Stonehouse “失踪”的背景。

sentences.en: He was on holiday in Miami in November of 1974.
sentences.zh: 1974 年 11 月，他在迈阿密度假。

sentences.en: He had had lunch with a business associate, and the pair had arranged to meet in the bar later that evening for a drink before dinner.
sentences.zh: 他和一位生意伙伴吃了午饭，两人约好当晚晚些时候在酒吧喝一杯，然后再吃晚饭。

sentences.en: Stonehouse had told his friend that he was going to go for a quick swim, and then perhaps do a bit of shopping for his wife and kids.
sentences.zh: Stonehouse 告诉他的朋友，他打算去游个泳，然后可能给妻子和孩子买点东西。

sentences.en: Afternoon turned to evening and his friend sat waiting in the bar.
sentences.zh: 下午变成了傍晚，他的朋友坐在酒吧里等着。

sentences.en: But there was no sign of Stonehouse. His friend asked around, and the last anyone had seen of him was at about 4pm, at the hotel’s private beach.
sentences.zh: 但 Stonehouse 踪影全无。他的朋友四处打听，最后有人看到他是在下午 4 点左右，在酒店的私人海滩上。

sentences.en: Stonehouse was in his swimming trunks, he had handed his clothes to an attendant, and waded out into the crystal clear water.
sentences.zh: Stonehouse 穿着泳裤，把衣服交给了一名服务员，然后走进了清澈见底的海水中。

sentences.en: And that was the last anyone had seen of him, until he was apprehended on the other side of the world, in Melbourne, just over a month later.
sentences.zh: 那是人们最后一次见到他，直到一个多月后，他在地球另一端的墨尔本被捕。

sentences.en: It’s now believed that he swam a little out into the water and then swam along the shore to the beach of another hotel, retrieved his “getaway kit”, which he had stashed earlier, and then made a beeline for, he rushed to, Miami airport.
sentences.zh: 现在人们认为，他先向海里游了一小段，然后沿着海岸游到另一家酒店的海滩，取回了他早先藏好的“逃跑装备”，然后直奔迈阿密机场。

sentences.en: He had a series of fake identities which he had created from recently deceased members of his constituency, so he was able to get onto flights undetected.
sentences.zh: 他利用选区内最近去世的选民身份伪造了一系列身份，因此能够神不知鬼不觉地登上飞机。

sentences.en: And when he was finally apprehended in Australia, he insisted that he'd done nothing wrong.
sentences.zh: 当他最终在澳大利亚被捕时，他坚称自己没做错任何事。

sentences.en: He said that he had been suffering a psychotic “episode” in which he was trying to escape the problems at home and that he had tried to commit “psychiatric suicide”, killing the identity of John Stonehouse and resurrecting himself with a completely new identity.
sentences.zh: 他说自己当时正处于精神病“发作”期，试图逃避国内的问题，他试图进行“精神自杀”，抹杀 John Stonehouse 的身份，并以一个全新的身份重生。

sentences.en: Few people bought this excuse. After some tense diplomatic negotiations, he was eventually extradited to Britain in July of 1975, 8 months after he was found in Melbourne.
sentences.zh: 没几个人相信这个借口。经过紧张的外交谈判，他最终于 1975 年 7 月被引渡回英国，这距离他在墨尔本被发现已经过去了 8 个月。

sentences.en: And there was this utterly bizarre situation in which he was both on trial for the crime of conspiracy, fraud and theft AND acting as an MP, a member of parliament.
sentences.zh: 于是出现了一个极其荒诞的局面：他一方面因阴谋、欺诈和盗窃罪受审，另一方面竟然还在担任国会议员。

sentences.en: Under normal circumstances, the Labour party would have most likely dismissed him immediately, but they had a very small majority in parliament, a majority of only three MPs.
sentences.zh: 在正常情况下，工党很可能会立即开除他，但当时他们在议会中仅占微弱多数，只比对手多三个席位。

sentences.en: It was a very tense situation, and although he might have committed a serious crime, they couldn’t risk losing him as an MP otherwise they risked losing political power.
sentences.zh: 局势非常紧张，尽管他可能犯下了严重的罪行，但他们不敢冒失去他这个议员席位的风险，否则就有失去政权的危险。

sentences.en: Stonehouse clearly thought he was going to get away with it, and he even proudly announced at his criminal trial that he didn’t need to be represented by a professional lawyer.
sentences.zh: Stonehouse 显然认为自己能逃脱惩罚，他甚至在刑事审判中自豪地宣布，他不需要专业律师为他辩护。

sentences.en: Despite having no legal training, he was going to represent himself.
sentences.zh: 尽管没有受过法律训练，他还是决定自我辩护。

sentences.en: It didn’t work. He was found guilty and sent to prison.
sentences.zh: 这没起作用。他被判有罪并入狱。

sentences.en: And this had knock-on consequences for British politics.
sentences.zh: 这对英国政坛产生了一系列连锁反应。

sentences.en: It meant that he had to resign as an MP, Labour lost its majority and had to form a coalition with the Liberals, which–some argue–cleared the path for Margaret Thatcher’s route to power.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他不得不辞去议员职务，工党失去了多数席位，不得不与自由党组成联合政府。有人认为，这为 Margaret Thatcher 的上台铺平了道路。

sentences.en: He ended up serving just three years in prison, and was released early because of good behaviour and health problems.
sentences.zh: 他最终只服刑了三年，因表现良好和健康问题提前获释。

sentences.en: He died in 1988 at the age of 62, and to his last breath he insisted that he had done nothing wrong, and that he certainly had not been a Czech spy.
sentences.zh: 他于 1988 年去世，享年 62 岁。直到临终前，他仍坚称自己没做错任何事，也绝不是捷克间谍。

sentences.en: Whether this is true or not, I cannot tell you, but what is undoubtedly true is that this is the story of a man who could have had it all, perhaps would have had it all, but managed to blow it in the most spectacular fashion.
sentences.zh: 事实究竟如何，我无法告诉你，但毋庸置疑的是，这是一个本可以拥有一切、或许本该拥有一切的人，却以最惊人的方式把一切都搞砸了的故事。

sentences.en: He said he'd been overwhelmed and had created a parallel personality for himself.
sentences.zh: 他说自己当时不堪重负，为自己创造了一个平行人格。

sentences.en: It certainly seems that he had lost all grip on reality.
sentences.zh: 看起来他确实已经完全脱离了现实。

sentences.en: He assumed that he could keep both his marriage and his lover, that he could start a new life for himself unnoticed, that he could simply “kill” John Stonehouse and re-emerge as Clive Mildoon.
sentences.zh: 他以为自己既能维持婚姻又能保住情人，以为自己可以悄无声息地开始新生活，以为自己可以简单地“杀死” John Stonehouse，然后以 Clive Mildoon 的身份重新出现。

sentences.en: Perhaps the greatest example of his losing all grip on reality was that he thought he would get away with it.
sentences.zh: 也许他脱离现实最典型的例子就是，他竟然认为自己能瞒天过海。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on John Stonehouse, the potential future prime minister who faked his own death.
sentences.zh: 好了，以上就是今天关于 John Stonehouse 的全部内容，这位曾有望成为首相却伪造了自己死亡的政治家。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这一集很有趣，也希望你学到了一些新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对这一集的看法。

sentences.en: Are there similar stories of politicians getting into trouble and resorting to desperate measures in your country?
sentences.zh: 在你的国家，是否有类似的政治家陷入困境并采取极端手段的故事？

sentences.en: You can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接前往我们的社区论坛 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他好奇的心灵一起交流。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是 Leonardo English 的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝大家平安，我们下期节目再见。
